text.p: These are the leading stories in the Turkish press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Justice minister expected to make a statement on Friday on investigations into a security scandal.
- Businessman husband of Foreign Minister Tansu Ciller says main opposition leader Mesut Yilmaz needs psychological treatment for having accused him of involvement in the murder of a casino owner.
- Ruling Islamist left on their own as coalition partner sides with opposition parties in parliament over universities and parliamentary immunity rights.
- Directorate General of Religious Affairs publishes fatwas to help people through their daily lives.
- State forces 100 people to join anti-rebel village guards system in southeastern town of Lice.
- Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan determined to privatise Turk Telekom.
- Turkey commemorates the 23th anniversary of the death of its second president Ismet Inonu.
- Islamist businessmen's organisation planning to form a cotton union between Turkey, Pakistan, Ozbekistan and Turkmenistan. These states produce 25 percent of cotton in the world production.
